children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my daughter Alex. She's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your daughter Alex, who is 11 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your living arrangement with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Can you tell me who Alex currently lives with, and do you make any financial contributions towards her upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She lives with her mum. Yes, I do contribute financially - I help out with things like clothes, school expenses, and other things she needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility properly, I need to understand the amount you're contributing:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or as a lump sum)?**

For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child, and £16.95 per week for additional children.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards her upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just one more important question:

**Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for her?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, her mum isn't claiming it, and nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex meets the age requirement**: She's 11 years old, which is under 16
- **You're considered responsible for her**: Even though Alex lives with her mum, you contribute £50 per week towards her upkeep (clothes, school expenses, etc.). This is more than the current Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child
- **You live in the UK**: You meet the residence requirement
- **No one else is claiming**: Alex's mum isn't claiming Child Benefit for her, and neither is anyone else

Under UK Child Benefit rules, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for a child who lives with someone else, as long as you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep. Since you're contributing £50 per week, you meet this requirement.

**Important note**: Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. Since no one else is claiming for Alex, you're free to make a claim. However, if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.
